texts.text: Few mandatory models hide the weakness of the faction

Themes, like events that grant scenario points, are often too powerful or can ruin the game. Themes that place too much emphasis on ronin also strip the faction of its character and make the lists a bit too generic. You see these big ronin profiles everywhere.
Not played in a long time so my impression may be outdated but open list feels very good you bring two one better for each scenario. Also ninja are just hard to beat
Pioson blood of orachi for Ito, and i always get swarmed by Savage wave, im sure i can beat it though with more practice

We're seeing too many list concepts centered around out-activating your oppoents. Clearly, Ryu and Awoken are the biggest offenders here. This needs to be reigned in to keep the game interactive and fun.

Feels like a big gap between old models and older themes vs new releases. Game development is great but something like Initiation Monks, while decent, feels like a very different game to modern releases. This doesnt mean everything should have a packed card (beginner friendly is good!), but some older areas of the game dont have the option to add some of that more complex depth - a release or two (or a rerelease) might boost some of these and refresh them noticeably.

Mostly the Models, I'm strongly for more restricted themes with stronger bonuses the 3 E&M Hunting pack and BGSP are actually good Exempels of themes ware this is done good. It's a Liddel sad that most of the time even 1 batter moddel in some factions makes me bracke theme.

Loads of NPE. The activation and pass token spam is not fun. Inability to do anything against a 4 armor samauri. Even Oni bring the same number of models with a much higher likelihood of higher health pool and survival
Open rebellion needs more models, as ataka. They are missing some options.
Too much Powerhouses. Only 1-2 counterlist to this Powerhouses.
Non-interactive lists like Descension prison, bakemono zoo, villagers kawas+byiba combo

Open Rebellion Shiho have good synergies to have good melee exchanges but often require crowding out models, which can be tricky to also play scenario. Having limited access to dealing with high armor and durable models can make leveraging melee exchanges quite difficult.
Matches often dont feel like they are about meele fights anymore. Often times its just who can out bullshit the other one more.

I don't play the prison list or Buzenbo but I'm trying to judge based on the peak of the faction. I think that the tribesmen and Karasu themes could use some love.
A bit to much soulless lists.

Use of Ronin in a faction as the best list, making the faction feel empty. Buzenbo in general and other models that just make a feel bad game where decisions are lowering loss rather than finding gain. (Others are Yuyukoma, Master Shi/Shikaku, Fuwa Kaiden, Akari to a degree, Villagers in general)

Hozumi is basically an autopick in most of the factions. Lots of op/underwhelming profiles. Toxic interactions (Haiatake prison, Akari activations spam, Prefecture pass abuse, Ryoka Sha not allowing opponent to use the activations he gives and many more). Cross faction balance needs work: Kinshi, Imperials, Shiho, Horselords are nowhere near the levels of Temple, Prefecture, Descension or Cult
Mainly quality of life, not balancing issues (the game is in a great state) - some individual overperforming or underperforming models, themes or cards

Bastions can play into almost any match-up and any scenario, to a point that all other themes are redundant. Hunting pack generates enormous amount of ki to a point where the player doesn’t ever have to worry about it. And the vengeance from the theme bonus lets you deal with all dangerous models one by one without big problems. Hozumi family at this point is just a simple solution to whatever problem you might have, giving you a ton of extra ki in addition.

Hard counters and negative play experiences. Factions, unique effects, and abilities that stop a player/opponent from interacting. For example Pre-ordained. Also, too many locations for rules - printed book, errata document, tournament booklet, campaign booklet, FAQ, some answers only on discord. So overall both mean this game is catered to experienced players in the game, and is not new player friendly

Hozumi and Kiyozumi are far too available and capable, Temple gains so many benefits from just being able to play all their models in what ever variation they so desire with all of their available stacking buffs, and Bekmono Hunting Pack has such a strong and straight forward gameplan that while hard to play, when played to the highest extent creates a very uninteractable negative play experience in my opinion. As for the weak themes, I feel almost any jung theme could have been put there other than Deep and Queen of the Waves, but my reason for finding Jung weak is not neccesarily the themes its the models, same with Shiho, the themes are not inherently awful, its the models that they have available for said themes.
I don't think there are any huge problems the issue seems to be with game times not allowing the game to finish in closer matches
One of the many bugs within the system is range attacks against larger models. They just explode.

All the strong themes play to already high strength areas. The weak ones either do nothing, or offer side-grade benefits that are pretty tame. Conclave of Captains in particular is junk, especially as it locks you into a cycle.
Selection of model, access to Robin, and theme traits

Descension: The prison is strong, not necessarily the theme. This and Buzenbo are really lifting up the faction.

I think some themes are a bit off and over the top. If some themes would be fixes there could be a greater variety in list building. Also Ronin models are quite strong, in comparison with some faction models (Shiho) But altogether I think the current meta is mostly fine.

The immense amount of alpha striking the game presents, having been experimenting with different factions and wanting to experience my models, but every game begins with 'can I survive the dive bomb my opponent presents at the end of round 1, or at the very beginning of round 2' just isnt a fun play cycle in my opinion.
Strong benefits and the model variety that can be taken

Strong themes I think except for JRG. A great balance/diversity in models: strong though guys, lots of AC with Shatei/Animals, fun tricks and traps, great events and access to Hidden Agenda. Without having the feeling that it's to much. Finding the perfect balance yourself in list building and choosing between all these things is the hardest part. Weaknesses imo are Fear 6 squads (spiders, Cult) but even more so the hard hitters like Minimoto and Prefecture Samurai, HBM and the likes.

Hozumi - Flexibility with some nice benefits. Wrath of Red Sun - Worse than both Alpha's and Ring Of Fire in what it provides and disallows slaves which means it struggles to put enough activations in the list. Jade Rose - Very limited model selection should provide a larger benefit.

Ronin cards and models often outshine factiom basef ones and become prevalant. Cards like preordain, year of the risen sun and rice bale barricades dominate list set ups and lead to homogenisation. Bushido shines in it's faction playstyles and that should be rewarded as much as possible
Minimoto are strong in melee, but easily outnumbered, slow and they have their difficulties against special attacks/defences with moving their opponents like sidestep oder slam attack
Varied places to have to find rules & rulings
Some combinations seem too strong. The meta doesn’t leave a lot place for taking good looking models over well performing ones. That sometimes is boring.

The existence of soulless spam turns every model that depends on opposed ki tests, poison, or fear into a trap option. Also Hozumi Family handing out aloof turns every match into a kill match even more than it already was.
For Kinshi, free actions. Hunting pack, the summons and Vengeance is great. Temple Villagers are obviously very good, but I don't think the themes are the strongest part of these factions

Ro-Kan is "suffering" from model bloat and is at a point where going themeless is probably one of their strongest options. Themeless can cover virtually all matchup bases, the faction identity is extremely watered down - the only thing characteristic about temple is "bad at shooting" and "rarely gets rerolls for its own models". Aside from that, the opponent needs to answer vastly different threats like mobile foxes, sturdy Kongu / Sohei or Ki Feat dominance lists with ekusa / masters. The faction desperately needs to be split to regain clearer boundaries to its' identity, allowing for more design space. I'd suggest putting Monks and Villagers into one faction, Sohei and foxes in another.
NPE are left in the game

[Personal introduction removed.] So I was struggling a bit to figure out exactly what the criteria are to not foul the data so I thought I'd explain the thought process. For weak themes, sometimes I think a theme is strong or weak not because of the theme bonuses but due to the model selection. So for example I rate Landing Party low because both the theme and model selection is bupkus. For prefecture patrol/Wrath of the Red Sun, they have good model access but a naff theme that is outclassed by every other choice. For the strongest it is a similar problem in reverse. Also I would add Passing the Night for Ryu and Minkan Densho to Temple, they are quite evenly matched overall in terms of power. Something to consider: Often I feel it's not certain themes dominating, but individual themes being so much weaker than its peers. Exceptions exist, such as The Deep outclassing any other Jung theme with Queen of the Waves a distant second, everything else meme-worthy.
hunting pack, bastions, haiatake prison and too much hozumi lists.
Villagers are too powerfull
Bad game design

Many good model with powerfull shooter option but they are pretty frail so the error are costly. Yurei have lot of cheap and resistant model that make fight pretty hard. Minimoto while they are hardly damaged are slow and costly model that can struggle against Jung good movement and event

Overall, the game is quite well-balanced. I enjoy the *Bushido* wargame. There are a few broken elements, such as the villagers and the "zoo" (creature-heavy) lists. Some samurai are unfairly underpriced. Also, I don’t see how one can defeat the Ninja faction, aside from playing as one of a couple of specific other factions. They are the strongest faction in the game and need to be toned down. Otherwise, I’m happy with it—thank you!
Some broken themes like Villagers, Cage

I think the main problem with the current meta is that some factions have too many non-interactive mechanics or mechanics without counterplay, which makes it very difficult to play on factions without such mechanics even with equal skill of both players.

Strong themes: Finest Steel: Because it is the pure Baseline of Minimoto. It makes the strongest models (Samurai) better and excludes only the lesser played models of the Faction (Ashigaru). It allows for very different and strong builds while bringing no downsides. Finest Steel dominates to the degree that it feels like Minimoto only have one theme. The Legation will hopefully change this. The Deep: Dominates Jung in the same way Finest Steel dominates Minimoto. Bastions of the mountain: The inexplicable choise of having their OpG Last Stand benefit be activatable at instant speed. This turns it into one of the nastiest "gotchas" in the game against an opponent who don't see it coming. Masters of the art: Got rightfully nerfed, is still fantastic. Followers of Inari: Boosts and unlock the strongest Fox Options. Cult themes: Boosts and amplifies strong parts of the already strong faction. Weak themes: Eternal Legion: The theme is disarrayed and in parts, counters itself. It puts up darkness turn 1 which means that the Non-Unique Bai Qian can run up the table while the non-soulless models can only walk. This means that the Non-soulless models will be separated from the Bai Qian and have a harder time of supporting them. It allows the Fangshi to Focus as a simple action, which they will have to to to be able to hand Ki out to the Bai Qian, but doing so means that they can only walk 4" up the table turn 1 and will have to try and catch up to the Bai Qian in turn 2 to be able to give them support. The fact that the Fangshi will have to Focus turn 1 means that the Warden will have to stay back with the Fangshi since they don't generate Ki if they go more than 3" away from the Fangshi. There is also a problem building stable and diverse Bai Qian lists since doing so requires at least two Fangshi to guarantee a steady ki supply for the Bai Qian. The fact that you need to bring along a Warden for them is more than fine but the big problem is that it is at the moment impossible to bring three Fangshi into a list since there only exists one Warden. And even if you could bring three Fangshi and Two Wardens into a list you would not have enough Rice left for any Bai Qian (at the minimum the Warden/Fangshi would cost you 80 rice). The other weak themes I think are self-explanatory.
Pacifism (and other SP cards that leave almost no chance to avoid them), Preordain (the psychological bonus of having a 6 or 1 ready to swap in is way beyond that cost of 3 rice)

Overall, in all strongest themes, we can identify key superpowers that either disrupt the opponent’s game, represent an obvious counter‑choice, or are simply too strong for their cost. If we look at the list of weak themes, pirates work very poorly if you want to play as captains. The North Star provides mediocre bonuses and doesn’t allow you to compensate for activations with passes. The brotherhood theme is difficult to implement in the game in terms of its main bonus, and overall it’s very hard to put together a tournament‑ready list of 6 models, since they’re all very expensive.

Buzenbo I struggle with controlling idols against ninjas when I dont have Fudo. Urchins with lookout seem cool but theme lock me. Someone like wakaba with disguise usually just ignores mit 1 Ki stat shatei. Theyre hard for malosi to catch or minori to shoot. I like how tactical the games feel and I understand their profiles are expensive but boy are their models blessed with options. Ryu makes me not want to fight and play roses fan dancers or shonosuke. I think malosi is too strong not to play [personal reference removed] and I think in turn sts struggles with whatever malosi struggles with. I wish JRG was more like nightmares of jigoku.

I feel like awoken does not have good internal balance with some models being too good, eg Kuna and aiumi. And others being underwhelming (Hannah, most cultists and cheaper family members) or very niche like chinatsu who is amazing in idols but brings nothing in zone scenarios. Chinatsu also has a hard time poisoning anyone because a success zero is still effectively a "miss" due to how her text is written.
I would like to see internal balance in awoken addresses so I could feel good about fielding a larger variety of models. I also would like to feel like I need to rely less of fear.

Bakemono HP is very strong because it generates enormous amount of Ki for summons due 2-3 ki stat animals with very low cost, so it is extremely mobile and can use lots of summons. Way of the Ancient Warrior gives enormous buffs to the haiatake guards. Bastions have free traps every turn an Kawa No Rojins are too versatile.

Ryu and awoken outpass ninjas. They also have enough anti camo/sixth sense mechanisms. Temple just shits on ninjas. Foxes, masters, traps etc. Even for bleeding moon it is rough. Honorable mention to buzenbo, although I feel that's much more playable.

Soulless is still by far the best ability in the game, and can really warp a matchup - please consider splitting it into a physical trait (immunity to poison, bleed, some unique effects); and a mental one (immune frightened, opponent OKI immunity)
Synergies and allowed models
Not enough experience with themes
Mostly just shiho struggling. [Personal group history removed]

1- Some key model/mechanics are too impactful on list building (buzenbo, fear...). 2- Reliability of control ki feat : Some model need O.Ki to put a state token (so they are counter by model immune/resistant to O.Ki AND by model immune to state) when other just activate their ki feat and their effect happen with no counter for the opponent. More generally, I feel like model placement should be more a way to protect yourself from opponent action by breaking LoS but too much effect doesn't need LoS (like aura/pulse,...).
Weak against “tanky” factions. Weak against soulless unless I bring Jade Witch. Locks me into that card, no real reason to deviate or try something new

Very happy in general, there are some models in each faction that would be nice to bring up in power, there has been quite a lot of power creep lately, that's normal but I think it's actually better if the dev team can admit that, it's just the natural order of things.. Nothing like GW's intentional power creep, but it's good to address it. The playtesting team is doing amazing work and it's fantastic to see all the community engagement, Bushido is in a great place!! Peace!

Mechanically disjointed, control effects are conditional and rebate of ki from theme limited in scope compared to Joyless Smiles, and added penalty of the Jaakuna cultists resolve all of their poison t1. Kimura cultists need help and not supported by the theme (though the campaign rules would be great additions!)

Models with exceptional burst/precision damage can circumvent the Minimoto resilience. Also factions with higher mobility and speed or activation efficiency can avoid or delay fighting and thus not allow me to play to my strengths.
New models often release overtuned leaving older models in the dust. A few warbands (horse lords in particular) have a few autolose matchens.
Ito are fragile and "hit hard" except Minimoto hit much harder and don't actually take much damage from the Ito.

Jaakuna dependence on Poison for control effects, and Fear(X) for defense - so models immune to poison, fearless and Soulless models hose those effects - and the Family isn't functional enough to patch that 'gap' - especially as many of the above are also immune to control - as theme doesn't help their throttled ki generation.
Ryu being op, and doing the same as Minimoto but better
Themes that are restricted but give Liddel benefits and factions with no real variance in the restrictivnis of there themes.
I don't think there's a single core problem, more of a plethora of small issues that add up but are not super negative overall (especially since the Awoken nerfs)
Reliable fighters, strong list building, layered synergies vs reliability to use limited events, movement and to be abled to outduel the opponent

All kaizoku being 1 ki stat makes them very hard to use in the current meta. For a “swarm” warband the cheap Models are too costly for what they offer vs other factions. The Kanchos are all over costed (except Sen’in) for the same reason. The theme diversity is fantastic and offers a lot of interesting play ideas (why I chose Jung as my main), but suffers greatly vs OpKi, fear tests, and just by generally being weak (except for the top of the faction such as crabmen but who I would also argue are too expensive for their in-faction niche vs other factions).
BotD - 10+ extra ki (where each extra ki is costed up to 1 rice via events) and very high resistance to fear

Again, tough to boil this down to three factions each. I usually have certain list archetypes in mind that are easier/harder to deal with. So I need to assume the list pairing my opponent is bringing. It can change drastically depending on what lists you need to navigate. Example for SW, playing into RoF/Kamimono is very different to playing into Hunting Pack/RoF.

There may be too many overpowered Ronin profiles. But the current meta isn’t terrible either. And the annual errata are welcome. Besides, if we compare Bushido to other skirmish games, it holds up well. However, we should tweak the profiles a bit—or, more importantly, increase the diversity of profiles within the struggling factions. Long live Bushido!
List building feels somewhat rigid

Slow mobility. Get hit and hit back way harder. Strong against targeted opposed ki feats. We survive A LOT most factions struggle to face a minimoto samurai or even damage him strongly The problems are durable models (due to low model count and very limited combo attack) Simply even better fighters, since Minimoto has no good way to support each other (only encountered that problem with Ryu, but damn that's rough)

The key problem is the presence of models or mechanics that can completely break the game on the opposing sheet. Again, I’ll give an example of a sheet with an ice mage on minimoto versus ninjas. While the ninja is closing in, the mage will simply shoot some of the ninja models with his magic via the ice kami. And then the Big Bear will come, scare them, and that will be the end of the game for the ninjas.

Temple villagers and temple as a whole due their variety in model selection. "Fun" themes which will never get taken Like Kimura, landing party, benthic servitude. Lack of more options in the newest factions. Haiatake Prison

Some faction intern balances seem to forget a few model types. Example given: Minimoto Samurai, Shugenja, Kami, bears are good. Blacksmiths are hit or miss. Ashigaru I feel a bit boring and clearly too expensive.

I think there are no best match ups, KKZ are doing fine in most cases. Their low model count paired with no own re-rolls makes them very susceptible for a downward spiral after failing an important roll early game. They struggle especially against easy available Sixth Sense, Webbed Ground, the insane tankyness of Minimoto and highly mobile fighters who can get Sixth Sense for shooting or melee with a Virtue effect.
Synergies with broken profiles. For Hozumi, it's the free Ki and Aloof every round, and natural synergy with every faction that has access to the best ronin models.
The models it allows you to take.
Strong- High movement and uninteractability. Weak- Lack of Model Support
Villagers, Minimoto Ice Spam, Ninja Swinginess, Preordain and must-include cards. Also: internal faction balance and games ending once one side has been wiped instead of finishing.
House of bleeding extra activation on very strong models that are not able to be interacted with.
Entire Factions are invalidated by a Single Model or keyword (Minimoto with Blizzard vs Horsegirls) (Ninja vs Buzembo or Kitsune with Sixth sense)

Ryu has a bunch of wait wait wait alpha strike lists that are all good but in combination with believer on hida it unlocks a bunch of nasty stuff. Imagine matsu under believer and unforeseen for extra ki on 3 activations arcing through horaki end of turn. Pew pew pew. Bastions has some really degenerate stupid gameplay with the traps and sapping silt kami and perhaps even more ki than the bakemono variant. Prison has to go or change the rules that you can at least pass and don't lose all your activations with no valid action to make.

What explains your faction’s strengths, weaknesses and matchups? (Optional) Kinshi don't feel like they have many really good or really bad match ups, very middling. Best probably against high cost/lower numbers where activation stealing through Ku/Shi is worth more. Feel worst against soulless/high ki factions where Void Stares Back/Contemplate don't work. Also lists that can engage early and hard which is less a faction thing and more a list thing. Ito, Ryu, Savage Wave and Horses can all do it. I feel like Zenith of the Void might be a little weak and really requires Ku for agency in your void counter generation. Even with Ku it's relatively easy for opponents to prevent 4 VC's till end of turn 2 or start of turn 3. Suggest moving Ki's first damage generates a VC to the theme (specify melee if power concerns but ranged may well be OK). Many factions are able to threaten portals on turn 1-2 via fast movement, scout and flank. Placing portals conservatively can mitigate this somewhat but then their power is also limited and weakens the theme. Too easy to destroy once in base to base, a wait action to remove 1/3 of a theme is harsh. Suspect this theme (and Imperial Court) needed some thinking when terrain destruction changes came in. Everything and Nothing seems much better, agency in VC generation and activation economy. Slower portals can be a drawback but also protects them from the aggressive plays mentioned above. Melee movement mostly being on attack makes disengaging difficult/dangerous (much worst than temple) and the faction is mostly pillow fisted so you can’t fight out of combat. Not necessarily a bad thing but worth mentioning. Hard to 3-0 games due to starting slow or being beatdown makes winning an event really hard. Batsu struggles to find a home, I’d prefer new Death Sentence synergy be added to the faction to create new vectors of list design but otherwise lower cost and/or remove/change that ability. Limited faction sounds good as an idea on paper but Kinshi will only ever really fall behing without release. Would like a faction card pack with a new theme and consideration for new miniatures down the line.

Balance of points, comparing things across factions is difficult because of different abilities they may have access to, so when something seems crazy cheap for one faction there may be reasons why. But within a faction there can be a clear better choice, and the factions that have the most 'strong choice' models tend to be the ones that see most play. Oh and crit attack #memes
Against other Samurai-Warbands I often succeed, against warbands with many ways to prone or trap, I struggle.

I am currently enjoying playing Ring of Fire and big Oni out of Savage Wave. And while the activation game hurts with the lower model count, the games have been fun with the exception of gimmicky lists like skeletons, rats or reactive lists made to play around melee, like Roses can sometimes be a bit frustrating. I was also a big fan of ninja's but could never properly execute with them, the low model count and the unforgiving nature of ninjas caused me to move over to Oni, who could actually take more than a few punches.

If asked a year ago I would have said celestials and their warping of the meta as well as the Awoken Fear and Destiny's Fear lists. Since the fantastic fix of them both in the (excellent) errata I feel the meta is in a quite good place. The biggest problem I see is that at a competitive level some factions get reduced to one or two strong lists/themes. It feels less like your playing against Minimoto than against Finest Steel or less like Facing Jung than the Deep. I would like to see/face a more diverse set of lists. This is a minor problem since all competitive games faces the same challenge.
For Templer: Extreme flexibility

There are some big outliers in terms of themes and profiles that lead to bad experiences, but I know some of these are being looked at. Haiatake Prison is crazy, Kuna is far too powerful, Masaru as well. Buzenbo is a problem, Kamuy is too. Kamuy is a good example that also limits list building a lot in Minimoto. No one has played anything but Blizzard successfully this past year. Card bloat is becoming an issue too. The unique effects are part of what makes Bushido a great game, because of the flavour it brings to each character, but the interactions have become so complex that they need too many words to explain. Some rules and rulings also don't help new players get on board when they seem unintuitive. The game is big and complicated now, and we could do with looking at these things again

For the Yurei cult, each of the listed themes can be incorporated into your deck, as they exhibit strong synergy with one another. For the Prefecture Each of these themes provides a wealth of resources for your miniatures, allowing you to assemble the right models to create powerful combinations. For the temple: I would single out the "bastions" theme as the only truly strong one; while the others are well-balanced, the bastions theme currently allows for the creation of the most powerful roster in the game.

The current meta of releasing miniatures and then nerfing them in a few months (e.g Passing the Night, a lovely theme box I enjoyed playing as-is until people started to use samurai outside of the theme box and now playing the box as-is is a horrible pain in the ass) or even before release (Shōgo‑Ryu). Or making a miniature completely unavailable for a faction without any warning, RIP my Void Toad. The last one was some Games Workshop level bullshittery I have never experienced elsewhere.

The strongest factions against ninjas have good access to sixth sense, but also other tricks to engage ok their terms (eg. Qimmiq and his places). Ninjas are best into factions that can't do much about camo, are less mobile (or lose their mobility advantage, like Horse Lords vs camo). HBM is also a very strong combination of hard to target and hard-hitting, usually with at least 6 tireless activations that swing the balance

Against the Pirates, Shiho, and the Syndicate as a whole, every ninja can counter with fairly strong abilities and always be confident that they will be able to rely on camouflage. In the case of the minimoto, the temple, and the birds, there are a lot of mechanics that break the key ninja mechanics. I pay a huge cost for each ninja for their camouflage, but then I encounter a bear, an ice mage, a leaf on sixth sense (near the temple), or birds that can simply ignore your camouflage and block and kill models with impunity.
Frequent releases with new gme mechanics, some list need a special counter list

Steam roll lists that hard counter core mechanics. Erosion of core mechanics like unkillable models in Cult, prison (Descension), unlimited activations (Ryu) or outwaiting your opponent and then playing your turn (Ryu and Akari). Preordain taking away the core mechanics of rolling dice. Scoring cards (events) that circumvent the core score mechanics. in a you go I go system these are sticking out to me. Basically any list/card that changes all the foundations of movement, combat and especially scoring in the game are really not fun at all
Pass tokens and ronin tricks

Can take Ronin

The game comes down to how good does your list go into another list. Overall faction strength change so quickly with additional models that are vastly superior to previous releases. E.g. savage wave best lists are two themes that are released recently where many models are unplayable. [Identifying play-group and event history removed.] The game needs a new edition.
Not familiar enough with these. Just know I have a rough time with those factions
Some themes/ sub factions clearly lack against the top lists.

Finest Steel "limits" you to the best profiles of the faction and also adds very powerful bonuses. Bastions of the Mountains forces you into Villager Spam but that is a viable strategy with really powerful benefits. House North Star, Open Rebellion and Conclave of Captains have far too weak effects for the hefty limitations on unit choice they force on you.

Too many hard counters or very skewed matchups (mostly caused by binary abilities). Eg, souless shuts down O.ki/ fear/ poison lists, camo removes interaction for all bar a few models (consider making spotting range variable (add Ki value?)), Imperial Court Statues vs lists with terrain destruction, Horselords into Minimoto due to Blizzard/damage mitigation, ranged damage spikes against large targets (unless they were lucky enough to get ranged defence), Descension prison (especially hurts against Kinshi where you can't move or kill the birds easily). 2 lists helps but often just pushes people towards a Ronin list that isn't really your faction. Activation and pass markers need careful valuing. Some expensive models don't do enough to warrant dropping 2-4 activations in your list (eg. Oni (2 activations vs Jun and 2 Slaves (6 activations)). Generation of extra activations and pass markers can leave you unable to counter enemy that abuse them (eg, Ninja heavy on pass can often wait til you're activated and then kill something important, thematic but feels really unfair when camo keeps them mostly safe. Games are often over end of turn 3/start of turn 4 (either due to time or due to one side being beatdown) and games are then played out in the mind rather than on the table. This is very anti-climatic. If this is the case could scenarios be shortened to 4 turns (VP/SP would need balancing). If you table someone you should get the remaining VP that could be scored, for now people can basically table with the exception of one mini they tie up. Just end the game and the pain. Pre-ordain and other dice manipulation, too good. One card has shut down my Kinshi because Ku was given bad dice or opponent good dice. Winner models are cool but widen the gap between top and bottom faction. They shouldn't be used to "fix" factions (a suggestion in the Savage Wave group) as you just create must take models. Imperial Court new Earth Fangshi and spoilt Warden are too similar to the existing version, I understand that's partly the theme but it's anti-climatic to see new releases for them. A lot of the above is much worse from a new players perspective and I have had friends drop the game due to the number of times we played a game where one sides rules impacted the others more than is reasonable. Experience might narrow that gap but you lose players. Advice given in discord was discuss the type of game but new players don't know and shouldn't be penalised because their theme box struggles into specific match ups. 1. Fear doesn't work. Most models that see play have bonuses for resisting fear, high Ki stats, or the "Fearless" trait. Almost all Samurai have "Bravery." This ability is "baked into" the cost of the models, but it would be better if it weren't there at all—paying for it is a waste. 2. Inflated model costs. This is again due to their abilities, many of which, unfortunately, don't actually work. There are plenty of Samurai in the game costing 16–18 Rice that come with 4 dice and powerful abilities, while the Yurei faction has models like Yama Uba, who costs 19 Rice... Have you ever seen her in a tournament, or even in a casual game? There are many such examples; no point in listing them all. In my view, some abilities simply need to be reworked—especially Fear. 3. The themes aren't bad, but the narrative component—which grants a bonus on the 4th turn—is extremely uncompetitive. In this game, turns 2 and 3 are usually what decide the outcome; I need the theme bonus to be active during those turns, not on turn 4. 4. Orphans... they are the most useless models in the game. If we want to summon a full-fledged Kami, we have to do it by turn 2. Meanwhile, you have to keep the child tucked away in the back so they don't get killed immediately. As a result, the Kami only arrives where it’s needed by the end of the third turn and doesn't start doing anything useful until turn 4. By that point, the game is often already decided. 5. Why was the "Bodyguard" ability removed from the Skeletons? It was the only way to protect the "squishy" Sisters.
